content.title: Who are some of the major industry partners for NASA's Artemis II?
content.text: Although NASA is leading Artemis II, much of the spacecraft and launch system has been developed by major aerospace contractors across the United States and Europe. Lockheed Martin (LMT) serves as the prime contractor for the Orion capsule, building both the crew module where astronauts will live during the mission and the launch abort system designed to pull the capsule away from the rocket in an emergency. Boeing (BA) is responsible for the core stage of the Space Launch System rocket, including its fuel tanks and onboard flight systems. The company also manages the upper-stage propulsion element that provides the final boost sending Orion toward the Moon. Northrop Grumman (NOC) supplies the twin solid rocket boosters that generate the majority of thrust during liftoff, as well as key components tied to the capsule’s abort system. Through the European Space Agency, Airbus (EADSF) (EADSY) built the European Service Module, which sits beneath the crew capsule and provides propulsion, electrical power, temperature regulation and life-support resources such as water and oxygen. Engine systems for both the rocket and spacecraft are provided by L3Harris Technologies (LHX), including the main engines derived from the Space Shuttle program and additional propulsion systems used for maneuvering in space.
